newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM investors see chance to buy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/IBM investors see chance to buy.

text.p: Option investors and traders were viewing a sharp selloff in International Business Machines Corp shares as a short-term buying opportunity, traders said Wednesday.
"Overall, traders feel that the low this morning at 155 or so was a buying opportunity for the short term," said Jon Najarian, president of Mercury Trading in Chicago.
But he said the stock appears poised to eventually test the 150 region.
By 1045 CST/1645 GMT, shares of the computer maker were down nine at 159 in consolidated trading.
Consolidated volume topped 7.9 million shares and IBM was the most active issue on the New York Stock Exchange.
The stock fell to an early session low of 155 after the company reported fourth quarter earnings late Tuesday.
IBM's quarterly earnings rose to $3.93 a share from $3.09 a year ago and beat Wall Street's consensus estimate of $3.88.
But some options traders said the earnings still fell short of some expectations which, combined with the stock's recent climb, indicated a selloff was likely.
On Tuesday, the stock hit 170-1/8 intraday, not far from its all-time high of 175 reached in August 1987.

"It certainly looks like it wants to trade toward 150, so we might break through that low we hit this morning," Najarian said. "But overall I think a lot of folks are probably using it as a buying opportunity."
Several brokerage firms commented on IBM Wednesday morning. A few maintained buy ratings, some cut earnings estimates, some raised estimates and others raised long-term price targets.
Morgan Stanley raised its long-term price target to $185 a share but said the stock might be starting a near-term correction of 10 percent or more.
"Morgan's probably not too far from right," Najarian said.
The selloff created several opportunities for options investors and traders, as call premiums slid and put premiums surged, dramatically in some strikes.
The IBM February 155 put, the most active put with volume of 3,420, rose 2-3/16, or 140 percent, to 3-3/4.

On the call side, the most active February 160, with volume of 7,150, dropped 6-7/8, or 57 percent, to 5-1/8. The February 165 call, which traded 5,280 contracts, slumped 65 percent, or 5-7/8 points, to 3-1/4.
Harrison Roth at Cowen & Co said, "The traders took the stock's downturn and translated it to price appreciation on the puts and price defaults on the calls, appropriately."
Despite the sharp moves, volatilities remained fairly stable, in part because they had not surged ahead of the earnings. Traders said volatilities were up slightly Tuesday.
February at-the-moneys were trading with volatilities around 30 Wednesday morning.
"Normally you'd have volatilities expand ahead of the earnings. Instead they were dying on the vine," Najarian said.
(--G. Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
